claims.text: UNSW requires that students must follow assessment instructions regarding AI use, that what students present must be their own work, and that students must acknowledge all sources including AI as an external source using proper referencing.

claims.text: Under Section 6.1 of UNSW's Assessment and Feedback Procedure, the course outline will be published at least one week before the start of the teaching period and will specify for each assessment the allowed role of artificial intelligence and, where relevant, how it can be used. The procedure specifies phased applicability across teaching periods: effective generally from Term 3 2026, Semester 2 2026, and Hexamester 1 2027, with clauses 1.1–1.2 and 1.4 effective from 1 January 2027, and clauses 2.1–2.2 and 3.5–3.7 effective from 1 January 2028.

evidence.quote:
6.1.  The course outline will be published at least one week before the start of the teaching period and will include the following for each assessment:
purpose  learning outcomes  the allowed role of artificial intelligence and, where relevant, how it can be used  weighting toward the  course result   when the assessment task is due for submission and its submission instructions, or when the assessment task will be held  timing and type of feedback  whether it is a hurdle task  whether a short extension is available  whether a supplementary assessment is available.

topics.title: Privacy & sensitive data
topics.summary: UNSW's Information Governance Policy applies to students, researchers, research trainees, employees and affiliates; individual procedures may have narrower scope. additionalTopics.summary: UNSW manages academic integrity under the Student Plagiarism Management Procedure across five tiers: Poor scholarship, Minor, Moderate, Significant, and Serious. For Minor plagiarism, the rubric states that a mark reduction should not exceed 10% of the maximum grade available for the assessment task (from plagiarism rubric Appendix 3 footnote 4, not an absolute cap). School authorities manage Poor scholarship and Minor through Significant cases. Serious cases must be referred to the Conduct & Integrity Office (CIO) as potential student misconduct, with potential outcomes ranging from task/course failure to suspension or exclusion (not automatic penalties). Actions outside the outcomes available for a level require CIO approval, and repeated instances may also be escalated to student misconduct. For School-level outcomes notified under clause 4.3(a), an internal review request must be made within 20 business days of that notice and is limited to procedural fairness, not the merits. Serious cases follow the separate CIO process.

academic_integrity.en: UNSW manages academic integrity under the Student Plagiarism Management Procedure across five tiers: Poor scholarship, Minor, Moderate, Significant, and Serious. For Minor plagiarism, the rubric states that a mark reduction should not exceed 10% of the maximum grade available for the assessment task (from plagiarism rubric Appendix 3 footnote 4, not an absolute cap). School authorities manage Poor scholarship and Minor through Significant cases. Serious cases must be referred to the Conduct & Integrity Office (CIO) as potential student misconduct, with potential outcomes ranging from task/course failure to suspension or exclusion (not automatic penalties). Actions outside the outcomes available for a level require CIO approval, and repeated instances may also be escalated to student misconduct. For School-level outcomes notified under clause 4.3(a), an internal review request must be made within 20 business days of that notice and is limited to procedural fairness, not the merits. Serious cases follow the separate CIO process.
academic_integrity.zh: UNSW 依据《学生抄袭管理程序》将学术不端划分为五个层级：学术素养不足（Poor scholarship）、轻微（Minor）、中度（Moderate）、重大（Significant）及严重（Serious）。对于 Minor 抄袭，细则明确规定扣分应不超过该项评估最高可得分的 10%（源自抄袭细则附录 3 脚注 4，并非法定硬性上限）。学院负责处理轻微至重大层级的案例；严重案例移交品行与诚信办公室（CIO）按可能构成学生不端行为处理，处理措施（包括不及格、停学或除名）属可能裁定而非自动适用。超出对应层级可用结果的处理需经 CIO 批准，重复违规亦可转为不当行为程序。对于依据第 4.3(a) 条通知的学院层级处理结果，内部复核须在收到该通知后 20 个工作日内提出，范围限于程序公平而非处理结论本身；Serious 案件另走 CIO 程序。

academic_integrity.en: UNSW manages academic integrity under the Student Plagiarism Management Procedure across five tiers: Poor scholarship, Minor, Moderate, Significant, and Serious. For Minor plagiarism, the rubric states that a mark reduction should not exceed 10% of the maximum grade available for the assessment task (from plagiarism rubric Appendix 3 footnote 4, not an absolute cap). School authorities manage Poor scholarship and Minor through Significant cases. Serious cases must be referred to the Conduct & Integrity Office (CIO) as potential student misconduct, with potential outcomes ranging from task/course failure to suspension or exclusion (not automatic penalties). Actions outside the outcomes available for a level require CIO approval, and repeated instances may also be escalated to student misconduct. For School-level outcomes notified under clause 4.3(a), an internal review request must be made within 20 business days of that notice and is limited to procedural fairness, not the merits. Serious cases follow the separate CIO process.
